newsitem.title: FRANCE: Business chiefs want Italy in EMU - Romiti.
newsitem.headline: Business chiefs want Italy in EMU - Romiti.

text.p: Italian business leaders want Italy to be part of European economic and monetary union (EMU) and Italy does not need a devaluation of the lira to be competitive, Fiat SpA president Cesare Romiti wrote on Monday in French daily Le Figaro.

"I absolutely do not believe, and I know that my opinion is shared by a majority in the Italian business world, that devaluation of the lira can be the most efficient way to overcome our difficulties," Romiti said.
He said Italian business leaders wanted Italy to be part of Europe.
"No corporate chief wants an Italy out of EMU, none of them would think of trusting his development perspectives to rampant devaluations," he said.

"For my part, ever since I have had responsability for running Fiat, I have always clearly spoken in favour of Italy's full inclusion in Europe -- without that solid link, I think, indeed, that no lasting growth outlook can exist for our economy and for our society."
Romiti said Italy could not rely exclusively on cleaning up its public finances by an "intolerable" rise in fiscal pressure.
"We also have to think of growth, we have to try to give our economy back its momentum and dynamism," he said.
He said this meant Italy had to undertake deep structural reforms in retirement, health and public employment spending.
He also cited labour market rigidity, high payroll charges and state intervention in the economy as problems Italy needed to address.
Romiti said industrialists wanted a fully European, credible and strong Italy.

"But there is one thing that we industrialists do not believe in and that is a monetary unification realised by European economic authorities without taking account of the real economy of our countries, which would satisfy accounting criteria, but at the price of too heavy a fiscal load and maintaining intolerable rigidities," he said.
If this were allowed to happen, he said, "Europe would crystalise into a union based on an unemployment rate reaching socially, politically and economically unacceptable levels."
